evals.prompt: Every Friday at 5pm, remind me in this chat to submit my timesheet. Set it up, but do not call Helio APIs in this evaluation.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a simple one-shot-per-week message, drafts the reminder first, recommends at most lightweight validation, lets the user choose the depth, and does not invent a three-case benchmark for deterministic low-risk work.
expectations: Recognizes the request as an automation and preserves the exact Friday 5pm schedule.
Drafts or proposes the actual reminder message before discussing creation machinery.
Explicitly considers whether evaluation is useful and recommends skip or lightweight evaluation because the work is deterministic and low-risk.
Lets the user choose the validation depth instead of imposing a representative/boundary/failure matrix.
If rehearsal is skipped, distinguishes approved wording from unverified scheduled delivery.
Describes the automation as created disabled, with enablement gated on the user's decision

evals.prompt: Every weekday at 8:30am, send me a compact digest of urgent support tickets opened in the previous 24 hours. If there are none, don't wake me. Set it up but leave it disabled; do not call APIs in this evaluation.
evals.expected_output: Recommends structured evaluation because inputs vary and silence has meaning, while keeping the recommendation concise and user-adjustable. Covers representative, zero-result, and dependency-failure behavior plus a disabled rehearsal.
expectations: Preserves the exact 8:30am weekday schedule and produces a representative digest before formalization.
Recommends structured evaluation because the data varies and no-result behavior differs from failure.
Offers the recommendation as a choice rather than forcing the user through a test-plan questionnaire.
Covers representative, zero-ticket no-op, and unavailable or stale data cases with observable checks.
Uses a disabled rehearsal and transcript inspection before recommending enablement.
Describes the automation as created disabled, with enablement gated on the user's decision

evals.prompt: When Stripe sends a dispute over $5,000, email legal with the customer and charge details. Set this up for me, but only describe the work in this evaluation and do not create anything.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a high-risk signed-webhook automation and recommends strict evaluation: authenticated fixtures, idempotency, sandboxed/intercepted email, failure cases, separate trigger/run evidence, and no enablement until checks pass.
expectations: Chooses a signed Stripe webhook based on source capability and verifies the signature.
Recommends strict evaluation because the automation handles sensitive data and sends external email.
Uses fixtures or a sandbox and intercepts email rather than sending a real test message to legal.
Verifies stable fire_key idempotency, irrelevant events, invalid signatures, duplicates, and upstream failures.
Separates trigger-handler evidence from the disabled automation run transcript and does not enable until both pass.
Describes the automation as created disabled, with enablement gated on the user's decision

evals.prompt: I drafted the procedure for a weekday 8:52am US stock report at /Users/yori/.helio/runtimes/abc/procedure-stock-report.md. Set up the automation disabled. In this evaluation, describe the exact command transport only and do not call APIs.
evals.expected_output: Treats the local markdown file as a drafting source, not as the procedure value. Reads its contents, puts the complete markdown body in the --procedure element of an argv JSON array, uses the JSON file only as --args-file transport, and verifies the returned canonical procedure document before rehearsal or enablement.
expectations: Preserves the exact weekday 8:52am schedule and keeps the automation disabled.
Reads or describes reading the draft file and uses its markdown contents as the procedure.
Never passes the local .md path as the value of --procedure.
Uses a JSON argument array whose --procedure element contains the markdown body, with only the JSON path passed to heliox --args-file.
Reads the returned document_id and verifies that the canonical document contains the procedure body before rehearsal or enablement.
Describes the automation as created disabled, with enablement gated on the user's decision

evals.prompt: Create a disabled weekday executive market brief automation. The facts are objective, but tone and story selection vary between AI runs, so I want confidence it will be consistently useful. Describe the creation and evaluation loop only; do not call APIs.
evals.expected_output: Uses an approved direct brief as the quality baseline, defines observable fact/freshness/format checks while leaving tone to human review, repeats representative candidate runs to expose variance, grades only after execution, aggregates consistency and transcript findings, presents outputs to the user, and revises and repeats before enablement.
expectations: Produces or proposes an approved direct brief before formalizing the automation and treats it as the new automation's quality baseline.
Separates objective checks such as freshness, required facts, citations, and delivery shape from subjective tone and story-selection review by the user.
Runs the representative disabled candidate three times by default because nondeterministic consistency matters, while allowing fewer runs only with an explicit safety or cost reason.
Grades each run after execution with exact output or transcript evidence, then aggregates pass rate and consistency and analyzes variance, hidden fallbacks, and weak checks.
Shows representative outputs and the evaluation summary to the user, incorporates feedback, and repeats the loop before offering enablement.
Describes the automation as created disabled, with enablement gated on the user's decision

evals.prompt: 请帮我创建并配置一个自动化任务：Every weekday at 7am, compile a summary of the pull requests merged into heliohq/helio in the last 24 hours, grouped by author, and post it to this channel. Describe the automation you would create; do not call APIs in this evaluation.
evals.expected_output: Treats the user's English instruction as the authoritative language source even though a Chinese wrapper sentence surrounds it, and writes the automation name, description, and procedure entirely in English. This pins the original bug: an English instruction entering through the automation hand-off must yield English artifacts, not Chinese ones inherited from the wrapper text.
expectations: Treats the user's English instruction, not the surrounding Chinese wrapper sentence, as the authoritative language source — the wrapper text must not set the artifact language.
Writes the automation name in English.
Writes the automation description in English.
Writes the procedure document in English.
Preserves the exact weekday 7am schedule.
Procedure pins a bounded, cadence-derived read window (no unbounded read)

evals.prompt: The conversation so far has been in English. The user now writes: '每个工作日下午6点，把当天在客服频道里没有得到回复的问题整理成一份清单发给我。' Set up the automation; describe it only, do not call APIs in this evaluation.
evals.expected_output: Uses the Chinese instruction as the authoritative language source even though the room language is English: the automation name, description, and procedure are written in Chinese, while conversational replies to the user stay in the room language (English). Artifact language follows the instruction, not the room.
expectations: Uses the Chinese instruction as the authoritative language source even though the room language is English.
Writes the automation name, description, and procedure in Chinese.
Does not fall back to the room language, because the instruction is long enough to determine its language.
Keeps conversational replies to the user in the room language (English) while the artifacts stay Chinese.
Preserves the exact weekday 6pm schedule.
Procedure includes an explicit failure path distinct from the quiet no-result path

evals.prompt: Every Monday at 9am, 汇总 the previous week's 新增用户 and churn numbers, then post a short executive summary to the growth channel. Describe the automation only; do not call APIs in this evaluation.
evals.expected_output: Judges the mixed-language instruction to be dominantly English — English sentence structure and the majority of the content, with only a few embedded Chinese nouns — and therefore writes the name, description, and procedure in English (the decided dominant language) as one coherent language, not a split across two.
expectations: Judges the dominant language of the mixed instruction to be English.
Writes the automation name, description, and procedure in English, the decided dominant language.
Does not split the artifacts across two languages.
Treats the embedded Chinese nouns as vocabulary within an otherwise English artifact, not as a signal to switch the artifact's language.
Preserves the exact Monday 9am schedule.
Procedure pins the read window to one cadence period (previous week), not an unbounded read
